title: SEC: rotate and de-hardcode the agent-shell gateway credential
description:
## Problem

`modules/doom.d/modules/tools/agent-shell/config.el:45` contains a live LEGO AI
Model Gateway credential in plaintext, git-tracked since commit `8685a85`:

```elisp
"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL" "http://127.0.0.1:8787"
"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" "6a7f7bb5919644abbcc1e90caa69627d:5ltY…"   ; ~380 chars, <account_id>:<secret>
```

This contradicts the repo's own stated rule — commit `43fffae` says "The key
itself is not in this commit and is not in the repo", and the cutover notes in
`.scratch/ai-model-gateway-cutover/map.md:20-21` say "Nothing in `.scratch/` or
`modules/` may contain the literal key." This file is inside `modules/`.

Every other secret in the repo goes through one of: secretspec
(`secretspec.toml`, used at `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:97` as
`!secretspec get -f … LEGO_GATEWAY_API_KEY`), gopass
(`guix/home-configuration.scm:151-171`), or agenix (`secrets/secrets.nix`).

## Also wrong in the same block

`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is the literal `http://127.0.0.1:8787`. That happens to be
correct only because this aspect (`den.aspects.doom-emacs`, reached via
`den.aspects.workstation` at `modules/workstation.nix:10`) is included solely by
`modules/mahakala.nix:3`, and the Guix-side headroom container publishes
`127.0.0.1:8787:8787` (`guix/home-configuration.scm:225`). On macOS the same
logical port is `18787` (`modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:76`). Nothing states this.

## Work

1. **Rotate the credential upstream first.** The value in git history is burned;
   assume it is compromised. This step is the user's to perform — ask, do not
   guess.
2. Replace the literal with a runtime lookup. `agent-shell-make-environment-variables`
   takes strings, so the value must be resolved in elisp — e.g. read from
   `(getenv "LEGO_GATEWAY_API_KEY")`, or shell out to
   `secretspec get -f ~/.config/home-manager/secretspec.toml LEGO_GATEWAY_API_KEY`
   at session start. Prefer whichever keeps a missing secret loud rather than
   sending an empty header.
3. Replace the literal base URL with a value threaded from Nix. `modules/doom-emacs.nix`
   already generates wrapped binaries and files from Nix, so the config.el can be
   templated or read a small generated elisp/JSON file.
4. Note in the commit message that history still contains the old key.

## Acceptance criteria

- No credential material anywhere under `modules/` — verify with
  `rg -n '[0-9a-f]{32}:' modules/` (returns nothing) and by eye on the diff.
- A missing/locked secret produces a visible error in the agent-shell session,
  not a silent 400/401.
- `just check` passes; `just check-fmt` passes.
- The old key is rotated (confirm with the user before closing).

## Verification

```
rg -n 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN' modules/
just check
```

## Follow-on

Once `home-manager-<gateway bead>` lands, the base URL and the key reference
should both come from that aspect rather than being fixed here twice.

title: Fix proxy-chain: Apple container forwarder no longer answers on gateway IP
description: local-model-proxy crash-loops (1046 FATALs) because its startup gate probes http://GATEWAY_IP:18787/livez. Apple container's port forwarder accepts TCP on *:18787 but only services requests arriving via loopback, so the HTTP request is closed with no reply. Same breakage affects MPS_BASE_URL and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. Inter-container DNS is still absent, but headroom's container IP answers from both host and container, so resolve container IPs at proxy start instead of using published host ports via the gateway IP.
acceptance_criteria: 18788 listening; proxy answers; no FATAL in /tmp/local-model-proxy.err after rebuild; darwin.nix and gateway.nix comments corrected
close_reason: Verified fixed. Root cause: Apple container's forwarder accepts TCP on *:18787 but answers only loopback-originated requests, so the gate's probe of GATEWAY_IP:18787/livez could never succeed. Now resolves headroom's container IP from status.networks per start (took two attempts -- the first read a nonexistent [0]['networks'] key). Post-deploy: 18788 listening, /health returns 200, container up at 192.168.64.12, FATAL count frozen at 1269 after 1269 crash-loop restarts. darwin.nix and gateway.nix comments corrected with the measurements. Commits 81b0da5 and 42e1df0.

title: Verify tier routing and the agent-shell model ids on mahakala
description:
## Why

home-manager-0pr.3 landed one tier-routing module and folded the agent-shell elisp
into it. Everything about pi's output was proven byte-identical from darwin, but
two things can only be verified on mahakala:

1. **The elisp model ids changed.** config.el's OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU env vars went
   from `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1` / `-sonnet-4-6` to
   `eu.anthropic.claude-opus-5` / `-sonnet-5`. This is a real runtime change and
   the one part of 0pr.3 with no byte-identical proof behind it. The ids were
   confirmed correct against ~/.cave/agent/models.json, which reaches the same
   endpoint, but agent-shell itself was never exercised with them.

2. **The agent .md files change from regular files to symlinks.** The deleted
   activation script had rewritten each nix-store symlink into a regular file so
   it could patch it. Home Manager refuses to clobber an unmanaged regular file,
   which is why modules/pi-tiers.nix keeps `force = true`. That force is what
   makes the first switch work; it has not been exercised on mahakala.

## Verification

Deploy with `just deploy-mahakala-hm` (per AGENTS.md; do not run raw
home-manager).

- The switch completes without a 'would be clobbered' error on any of the seven
  ~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md.
- Those files are byte-identical to what was there before the switch. They were
  captured on 2026-08-01 as matching the reference-oracle output; if they differ,
  0pr.3's byte-identical criterion did not survive contact and the diff belongs in
  its notes.
- `~/.pi/agent/tier-defs.json` is unchanged and still contains the
  provider-native ids (openai-codex/gpt-5.5, opencode-go/kimi-k2.6,
  cursor/composer-latest) -- mahakala's pi does NOT route through the gateway.
- The doom-dir derivation builds: all five --replace-fail placeholders are
  present, so a renamed one is a build error rather than a silent miss. This is
  the first build of that derivation since the three model placeholders were
  added, and it cannot be built from darwin (x86_64-linux).
- Start an agent-shell Claude Code session and confirm it reaches a model rather
  than erroring on an unknown model id.

## Notes

Independent of home-manager-047 (the 0pr.2 gateway deploy) but touches the same
machine and the same Home Manager profile, so do them in one sitting if both are
still open.

title: Caveman Code's agent dir on mahakala is unmanaged and holds a hardcoded gateway key
description:
## Problem

`~/.cave/agent/models.json` on mahakala is hand-written and tracked by nothing in
this repo. It declares provider `lego-anthropic` against
`http://127.0.0.1:8787` (headroom's mahakala loopback, same address
modules/doom-emacs.nix substitutes into the agent-shell elisp) and embeds a
literal `vk_…` virtual key as `apiKey`.

That is the same credential class home-manager-0pr.1 remediated for the elisp and
launchd agents: a key as a literal rather than as a command resolved at
agent-process start. gateway.nix already exposes `keyCommand`, and pi's
models.json marks an executable lookup with a `!` prefix — Caveman Code is a pi
fork, so the same `!` mechanism should work unchanged.

Discovered while scoping home-manager-0pr.3. Caveman Code is the primary harness
on mahakala, so this file is more load-bearing than its unmanaged status implies.

## Why it is not part of 0pr.3

0pr.3 owns tier->model routing for pi. This is credential hygiene plus a
decision about whether ~/.cave/agent joins the managed set at all. Folding it in
would have doubled that bead.

## Shape to aim for

Decide first whether ~/.cave/agent is managed. If yes, it is a Guix Home or Home
Manager file on mahakala reading gateway.nix's keyCommand, and models.json needs
the same seeded-once treatment pi's has (modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix) so /model
can still re-point it live. If no, the key still has to stop being a literal.

## Acceptance criteria

- No literal vk_ key on disk in a hand-edited file on mahakala.
- The decision about whether ~/.cave/agent is managed is recorded, not implied.
- Verified on mahakala (requires guix home reconfigure / home-manager switch there).

## Notes

The key value was shared in a session transcript and is deliberately not
recorded here. Treat it as exposed and rotate it as part of this bead.

title: Apply and verify the gateway change on mahakala (guix home reconfigure)
description:
## Why this exists

home-manager-0pr.2 gave the model gateway one owner (gateway.json, landed in
0d2a5e7). Its darwin half is deployed and verified on M-02877. Its Guix half is
statically verified but **not applied**: nothing has run `guix home reconfigure`
on mahakala since the change.

This must run on mahakala. It cannot be done from the darwin workstation.

## What changed on mahakala's side

`guix/home-configuration.scm` no longer holds gateway literals. It reads
`~/.config/home-manager/gateway.json` at reconfigure time via guile-json and
derives the headroom container's image, published port, environment, and
`--port` argument from it.

**One intended behaviour change:** `HEADROOM_MODE=cache` is now set on mahakala.
It was previously absent, so mahakala silently ran headroom's built-in default
mode -- a different cost and cache-hit tradeoff from M-02877, which has had
`cache` set with a written rationale all along. This is the drift 0pr.2 existed
to kill.

## Steps

    cd ~/.config/home-manager
    git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main   # never `git pull`; main was rewritten
    just deploy-mahakala-guix                   # guix pull + guix home reconfigure

## Acceptance criteria

- `guix home reconfigure` completes without error. The reader is the risk: if it
  fails inside `gateway-ref`, `gateway-object-ref`, or `json->scm`, capture the
  full backtrace into this issue -- that is a seam defect, not a config typo.
- headroom comes back up and serves:
      curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8787/livez
      curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8787/readyz
  Allow ~3 minutes after start before trusting a failure; on M-02877 headroom
  needed roughly 190s of uptime before it answered.
- The running container carries the facts from gateway.json, `HEADROOM_MODE`
  included:
      podman inspect headroom | grep -E 'HEADROOM_|ANTHROPIC_TARGET'
  Expect exactly: HEADROOM_HOST=0.0.0.0, HEADROOM_STORE_URL=sqlite:////data/headroom.db,
  HEADROOM_SAVINGS_PATH=/data/proxy_savings.json, HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off,
  HEADROOM_MODE=cache,
  ANTHROPIC_TARGET_API_URL=https://api.genai.thelegogroup.com/claude
- The published port is still loopback-only:
      ss -lntp | grep 8787      # expect 127.0.0.1:8787, not 0.0.0.0:8787
- agent-shell in Doom Emacs still reaches a model end to end. That path also
  exercises the key-lookup command, which is the other thing only mahakala can
  verify (the remaining on-machine item from home-manager-0pr.1).

## Notes for whoever runs it

- Do not edit `guix/home-configuration.scm` to "fix" a value. Every fact it
  reads is owned by `gateway.json`; change it there and both substrates follow.
  See docs/adr/0001-gateway-facts-cross-the-guix-seam-as-json.md.
- The Scheme was validated against real Guix 1.5.0 in a container before
  landing, and the rendered `oci-container-configuration` differed from the
  pre-change file by exactly one line, `HEADROOM_MODE=cache`. Guix's guile-json
  returns alists rather than hash tables; `gateway-object-ref` handles both. If
  reconfigure still fails, that is new information worth recording carefully.
- Reproduction recipe for the container check is in
  docs/solutions/proxy-chain-and-harness-auth.md, under "verify a Guix-side
  change without mahakala".

title: Rust and kernel pins as data, not regex-anchored text
description:
## Problem

`scripts/update-rust-tools.sh` reaches into `modules/overlays.nix` through a
regex anchored on **eight literal spaces of indentation**:

```python
rf"(?ms)^        {re.escape(package)} = final\.rustPlatform\.buildRustPackage \{{.*?^        \}};"   # :48
r'(?ms)^        decapod = final\.rustPlatform\.buildRustPackage \{.*?^        \};'                   # :91
r'(?ms)^        rtk = final\.rustPlatform\.buildRustPackage \{.*?^        \};'                       # :126
```

Those eight spaces encode four levels of nesting — `den.aspects.devtools.homeManager`
(`modules/overlays.nix:6`) → `nixpkgs.overlays` (`:7`) → `(final: prev: {` (`:16`)
→ the package attribute (`:17`) — at two-space alejandra indent. The script also
hardcodes the attribute path `overlayModule.den.aspects.devtools.homeManager`
(`scripts/update-rust-tools.sh:112-124`) to re-derive `pkgs` for hash computation.

So the *interface* between the updater and the pins is a formatting convention
plus an attribute path. Any restructuring of `overlays.nix` — wrapping the list in
a `let`, splitting the overlay lambda, moving the pins — breaks `just update`
with `SystemExit("Could not patch decapod block")`. Loud, but a hard stop with no
fallback, and nothing in `just check` exercises the script.

Same shape, worse failure mode, in `scripts/upgrade-cachyos-kernel.sh`: it
assumes the **first** `(base32 "…")` in `guix-packages/linux-cachyos.scm` is the
CachyOS patches hash and the **second** is the kernel source hash
(`:52` uses `sed -i "0,/(base32 \".*\")/{…}"`, `:55-60` an `awk` counter). Insert
a third source above them and it silently patches the wrong hash — and no Guix
eval runs afterwards to catch it.

Within-file hand-sync also exists: `modules/overlays.nix:19` `version = "0.88.0"`
must match the crate URL at `:22`; `:211` `version = "0.44.1"` must match
`rev = "v0.44.1"` at `:214-217`.

## Shape to aim for

Move the pin data out of the overlay body into a data module — the interface
becomes data instead of text:

```nix
# modules/pins.nix  (or pins.json)
{
  decapod = { version = "0.88.0"; hash = "sha256-…"; cargoHash = "sha256-…"; };
  br      = { version = "…";      hash = "…";        cargoHash = "…"; };
  rtk     = { version = "0.44.1"; hash = "…";        cargoHash = "…"; };
  bv      = { version = "…";      hash = "…";        vendorHash = null; };
  agent-token-dashboard = { version = "…"; hash = "…"; vendorHash = "…"; };
}
```

`modules/overlays.nix` consumes it and derives every URL/`rev` from `version`, so
the within-file sync disappears. `scripts/update-rust-tools.sh` rewrites the data
file structurally (JSON is easiest to rewrite safely; a Nix attrset of literals
is also mechanically rewritable). Same treatment retires the base32 counting in
`upgrade-cachyos-kernel.sh`.

## Inventory of what lives in overlays.nix today

Distinct patterns, mostly used once or twice — worth knowing before you move things:

1. flake-input passthrough — `devenv` (`:8`), `pi` (`:9`), `omp` (`:13`)
2. rust source+cargoHash — `decapod` (`:17-46`), `br` (`:160-186`), `rtk` (`:210-232`)
3. go source+vendorHash — `bv` (`:187-209`, `vendorHash = null`), `agent-token-dashboard` (`:233-263`)
4. python application — `mcp-agent-mail` (`:48-158`); note its ~25-package
   `propagatedBuildInputs` list is re-typed verbatim inside the `postInstall`
   `makePythonPath` call (`:73-96` vs `:113-136`) — a second, smaller duplication
   worth fixing while you are in here
5. go.mod toolchain substitution duplicated across derivation and `overrideModAttrs` (`:250-262`)
6. scope override — `python313Packages.fastmcp` `doCheck = false` (`:266-269`)
7. `doCheck = false` on 6 packages with no per-package reason recorded

Only patterns 2 and 3 are in scope for this bead. Do not restructure 4-6.

## Acceptance criteria

- Version, source hash and cargo/vendor hash for each pinned tool appear exactly
  once, as data.
- Crate URLs and git `rev`s are derived from `version`, not re-typed.
- `just update-rust-tools` succeeds and produces an identical closure when
  nothing upstream has changed (idempotence check below).
- The updater no longer contains an indentation anchor or a hardcoded
  `den.aspects.*` attribute path.
- `scripts/upgrade-cachyos-kernel.sh` no longer relies on base32 ordinal position.
- `just check` passes.

## Verification

```
nix eval --no-warn-dirty --json .#homeConfigurations.worldofgeese.config.home.packages \
  --apply 'ps: map (p: p.name) ps' > /tmp/pkgs.before
just update-rust-tools     # with no upstream releases pending: must be a no-op diff
git diff --stat
nix eval ... > /tmp/pkgs.after && diff /tmp/pkgs.before /tmp/pkgs.after
just check
```
close_reason: Updater regex and base32 ordinal problems were already eliminated by later work; the remaining duplication (br/bv version re-typed as git tag) is fixed in a3d82bb. Each version and hash now appears once. No pins data module: no non-human consumer remains to justify it.

Already gone (verified 2026-08-27):

title: Derive just check from the entity registry; cover Guix, image, tofu
description:
## Problem

`just check` (`Justfile:57-72`) is the repo's only automated gate — the
pre-commit hook runs exactly it (`.githooks/pre-commit`). Every line of it is
hand-written, so coverage was decided per host by whoever last remembered.

| entity | what is verified | gap |
|---|---|---|
| `nixosConfigurations.paphos` | `config.system.stateVersion` (`Justfile:59`) | never touches the package list |
| `nixosConfigurations.oracle` | `config.system.stateVersion` (`:60`) | same |
| `homeConfigurations.worldofgeese` | every `home.packages` name (`:68`) | the strongest check in the file |
| `darwinConfigurations.M-02877` | `system.build.toplevel.drvPath` (`:69`) | weaker on the package axis than mahakala |
| `nixOnDroidConfigurations.pixel-fold` | `config.system.stateVersion` (`:70`) | never touches the package list |
| `guix/system.scm` | **nothing** | no Guile/Guix eval anywhere in the repo |
| `guix/home-configuration.scm` | **nothing** | 477 lines, only exercised by a live `guix home reconfigure` |
| `guix-packages/linux-cachyos.scm` | **nothing** | rewritten by `scripts/upgrade-cachyos-kernel.sh` with no eval afterwards |
| `packages.aarch64-linux.oracle-image` | recipe exists (`Justfile:133-134`) but is **not** called by `check` | |
| `terraform/oracle/*.tf` | recipes exist (`Justfile:139-143`) but are **not** called by `check` | |
| `scripts/*.sh` | no shellcheck, no dry-run, no tests | shellcheck is installed (`modules/shared-devtools.nix:11`) but never run |

The `stateVersion` strategy is known-insufficient and the Justfile says so: the
comment at `:66-67` explains that `stateVersion` "evaluates without ever touching
the package list", i.e. it would pass even with the exact `omp` overlay
regression the check exists to catch (`modules/overlays.nix:10-12`, fixed in
`c766dde`).

## Shape to aim for

`just check` becomes one line over a derived set of checks. The entity registry
(`modules/hosts.nix`) already knows every den-managed host and home, so per-entity
checks should be *derived*, not typed:

- expose `flake.checks.<system>.<name>` per `den.hosts` / `den.homes` entry
- one adapter per substrate for the eval strategy (NixOS → package names;
  darwin → package names or toplevel; nix-on-droid → package names)
- one adapter for Guix: at minimum `guix repl`/`guild compile` syntax+load of
  `guix/system.scm`, `guix/home-configuration.scm`, `guix-packages/linux-cachyos.scm`;
  ideally `guix home build`/`guix system build --dry-run`
- wire in `check-oracle-image` and `oracle-tofu-validate` / `oracle-tofu-fmt-check`

Adding a host should add its check with no Justfile edit. That is the leverage.

## Constraints and gotchas — read before changing eval strategy

- The comment at `Justfile:61-67` is load-bearing: doom-emacs builds via **IFD**,
  so forcing `activationPackage.drvPath` for `worldofgeese` on a darwin machine
  makes eval *build* `doom-intermediates`, which needs a real `x86_64-linux`
  builder that is not available. That is why the mahakala check forces
  `home.packages` **names** instead. Preserve that reasoning and keep it written
  down in the new module.
- `--no-warn-dirty` everywhere is deliberate (noise suppression during iterative
  checking).
- Guix checks must degrade to a skip when `guix` is absent (it only exists on
  mahakala), the same way `typecheck-pi-extensions` skips when `npx` is missing
  (`Justfile:74-82`). A check that fails on darwin because Guix is not installed
  is worse than no check.
- Do not make `check` require network or a remote builder; it runs in a
  pre-commit hook.

## Acceptance criteria

- `just check` still passes and still catches the `omp` class of regression
  (verify by temporarily deleting the `omp` mapping at `modules/overlays.nix:13`
  and confirming failure, then restoring).
- Package-list coverage exists for every den-managed entity, not just mahakala.
- Guix files are at least syntax/load-checked when `guix` is available, skipped
  cleanly otherwise.
- `check-oracle-image` and the tofu validators are reachable from `just check` or
  from a documented `just check-all`.
- Runtime of `just check` stays acceptable for a pre-commit hook; note the new
  timing in the issue before closing.

## Verification

```
just check                                  # passes
sed -i.bak '/omp = /d' modules/overlays.nix && just check ; mv modules/overlays.nix.bak modules/overlays.nix   # must fail
time just check
```
close_reason: Landed 721bad4: check is now derived from the configuration registry (modules/checks.nix), package-name coverage extends to all five entities, Guix files are load-checked when guix is present and skipped otherwise, and image/tofu are reachable via check-all. Timing recorded in the comment. Guix success path remains unverified until mahakala is reachable.

comments.author: Tao Hansen
comments.text:
Landed 721bad4: modules/checks.nix exposes flake.evalChecks, derived by mapping over nixosConfigurations / darwinConfigurations / homeConfigurations / nixOnDroidConfigurations. Per entity it forces system.build.toplevel.drvPath plus a sha256 digest of every Home Manager user's home.packages names. Justfile 'check' is now one 'nix eval --json .#evalChecks' instead of five hand-written per-host lines, so a new modules/hosts.nix entry gains coverage with no Justfile edit.

Coverage before -> after: paphos, oracle and pixel-fold were only checked via config.system.stateVersion, which never touches the package list; all three now get package-name coverage (oracle reports users:{} because it has no Home Manager module). Confirmed output covers all five entities: darwin.M-02877 (user dktaohan), nixos.paphos (user kypris), nixos.oracle, homes.worldofgeese, nixOnDroid.pixel-fold.

check-guix added: loads guix/system.scm, guix/home-configuration.scm and guix-packages/linux-cachyos.scm with 'guix repl -L guix-packages', and skips with a message when guix is absent. Only the skip path is verified here — darwin has no guix and mahakala is unreachable, so the success path is UNVERIFIED and should be confirmed on mahakala.

check-all added: chains check + check-oracle-image + oracle-tofu-fmt-check + oracle-tofu-validate. Kept out of the pre-commit path because tofu validate needs init state.

Regression test, corrected: the bead's suggested probe (delete the omp mapping at overlays.nix:13) is stale — no omp mapping exists in overlays.nix any more. Substituted renaming the 'br' overlay attribute, which shared-devtools.nix puts in home.packages. Result: 'nix eval .#evalChecks' exits 1 with 'while evaluating attribute homes / worldofgeese'. Same perturbation against the OLD strategy: the paphos stateVersion line still exits 0 (the gap this bead is about), while the old worldofgeese length line exits 1 — home.packages is a listOf package, so module type-checking already forces each element. The comment in checks.nix was corrected to say so rather than claiming length would have missed it. A first probe using 'devenv' was inconclusive because nothing puts devenv in home.packages.

Timing on M-02877 (warm store): 'nix eval .#evalChecks' 63s cold / ~25s warm; full 'just check' 2m1s, which includes check-doom-darwin and check-fmt. Commit through the pre-commit hook took 54s. Acceptable for the hook, but it is not fast.

title: One tier-routing module instead of two
description:
## Problem

"Which model does an agent tier use" is implemented twice, in two languages, at
two lifecycle stages, and the work profile force-disables the shared copy seven
times.

| | personal (mahakala) | work (M-02877) |
|---|---|---|
| tier table | `modules/pi.nix:71-87` (`tierDefs`) | `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:19-40` (`workTierDefs`, `workTiers`) |
| model ids | provider-native | `gatewayModels` at `:43`, LEGO gateway ids |
| frontmatter patch | Node.js script in `home.activation`, `modules/pi.nix:140-190` — runs at **activation**, reads `tier-defs.json` off disk | `patchAgentModel` via `builtins.replaceStrings`, `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:103` — runs at **build** |
| emitted file | `home.file.".pi/agent/tier-defs.json"` (`modules/pi.nix:71`, `lib.mkDefault`) | same path, `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:152` |
| overrides | — | `lib.mkForce` at `:175`, `:176`, `:199-205` (7 agent files) |

Agent definitions being patched: `pi-extensions/agent-overrides/{worker,planner,oracle,reviewer,scout,researcher,workstream-compounder}.md`.

**Deletion test**: deleting `modules/pi.nix`'s tier logic *spreads* — mahakala
never reads `dktaohan.nix`. Deleting `dktaohan.nix`'s *spreads* too. Neither copy
can absorb the other, which is the signal that a shared module is missing rather
than that one is redundant.

Churn evidence: `modules/pi.nix` (20 commits) and `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix`
(15 commits) are the two hottest Nix files in the last 120 commits.

## Shape to aim for

One module whose interface is a tier table plus a model table, and whose
implementation owns the whole transform:

```
pi.tiers = {
  tiers  = { fast = { … }; balanced = { … }; deep = { … }; };  # tier -> requirements
  models = […];                                                # profile-specific model ids
};
```

Implementation absorbs: tier→model resolution, agent-frontmatter patching,
`tier-defs.json` emission, fallback chains. Two adapters: the personal model
table and the gateway model table. Callers supply only a table.

Prefer the **build-time** patch (`replaceStrings`, as in `dktaohan.nix`) over the
activation-time Node script. Reasons: failures surface during `nix eval` / `just
check` instead of mid-activation on the machine; there is nothing the Node script
can see at activation that Nix cannot see at build time; and it deletes ~50 lines
of embedded JavaScript.

## Constraints and gotchas

- The work profile force-disables the shared `beads-rust` and `governance`
  extensions (`modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:175-176`). Those `mkForce`s are about
  extensions, not tiers — do not sweep them into this change.
- `pi-extensions/governance/index.ts` reads `globalThis.__beadsRustState`
  published by `pi-extensions/beads-rust/index.ts:207-214`. Both are deeper than
  their interfaces and are **not** targets here.
- `modules/pi.nix:39-42` documents that `pi-rtk-optimizer` pins
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ^0.74 || ^0.75` while the `pi` binary comes
  from the `llm-agents` flake input via `modules/overlays.nix:9`. Nothing checks
  that coupling. Leave the prohibition comment intact.
- Keep `tier-defs.json` at the same path — it is read by tooling at runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- One module resolves tier→model; each profile contributes only its model table.
- The Node.js activation patcher is deleted.
- Zero `lib.mkForce` on agent `.md` files remains for tier reasons.
- `~/.pi/agent/tier-defs.json` and every patched agent `.md` are byte-identical
  before and after on **both** profiles (capture baselines first — see below).
- `just check` passes.

## Verification

Capture baselines before touching anything:

```
nix eval --raw --no-warn-dirty '.#homeConfigurations.worldofgeese.config.home.file.".pi/agent/tier-defs.json".text' > /tmp/tiers-wog.before
nix eval --raw --no-warn-dirty '.#darwinConfigurations.M-02877.config.home-manager.users.dktaohan.home.file.".pi/agent/tier-defs.json".text' > /tmp/tiers-work.before
```

Diff the same expressions after. For the agent `.md` files, build the derivations
and `diff -r` the resulting store paths.
notes:
## Correction to this bead's problem statement

The problem table was wrong in one load-bearing way, and it changed the design.

It presented the activation-time Node patcher as the *personal* profile's
mechanism and patchAgentModel as the *work* profile's. In fact both ran on the
work profile: modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix includes den.aspects.pi and never
disabled home.activation.syncPiUserAgentModelOverrides. The activation script ran
last, so it decided what landed on disk on **both** profiles.

Evidence, oracle.md on M-02877 before the change:

| | model: | thinking: | field order |
|---|---|---|---|
| source agent-overrides/oracle.md | cursor/composer-latest | medium | model, fallbackModels, thinking |
| built store path | anthropic-proxy/...opus-5 | medium | model, fallbackModels, thinking |
| live ~/.pi/agent/agents/oracle.md | anthropic-proxy/...opus-5 | **high** | **model, thinking, fallbackModels** |

thinking: high and that ordering are only producible by the Node script.

So patchAgentModel was provably inert, not a second irreducible copy: running the
activation script over the raw sources and over the build-patched sources yields
byte-identical output, because it re-derives model from the same tier table and
rewrites the line regardless. Verified by extracting the script unchanged and
running it over both input sets.

**The deletion test is therefore asymmetric, not symmetric as this bead argued.**
One copy was dead weight masked by the other. A shared module was still the right
answer for the tier *table*, but the reasoning in the Problem section overstated
the case for the patcher.

Consequence for the design: the shared build-time patcher had to reproduce the
*Node script's* semantics (patch model AND thinking, re-insert both after
description:, which moves thinking above fallbackModels), not patchAgentModel's
weaker replaceStrings-on-model-only. Had it used the latter, oracle and reviewer
would have silently regressed from thinking: high to medium on the work profile,
and the personal profile would have lost tier-driven thinking patching entirely.

## Verification step reinterpreted, with agreement

This bead said to 'build the derivations and diff -r the resulting store paths'
for the agent .md files. Under the only behaviour-preserving design that check
**must fail**, because M-02877's store .md files never matched what was on disk
-- the activation script rewrote them after the fact.

Agreed with the owner before implementing: the **final on-disk file** is the
contract, and the store .md content is allowed to change. Recorded because a
future reviewer running the bead's literal verification command will see a diff
and should not read it as a regression.

## What the byte-identical criterion was actually tested against

The current activation script was extracted verbatim and used as a reference
oracle, run over the source overrides with each profile's tier-defs.json. Its
output was confirmed to match the live ~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md on M-02877
byte-for-byte on all 7 files, so the oracle reproduces reality rather than a
model of it. That output is the baseline the new build-time patcher was diffed
against.

Results:
- tier-defs.json: byte-identical on both profiles.
- All 7 agent .md: byte-identical on both profiles (14/14).
- pi models.json: unchanged, same store path (35ly04gj...-pi-models.json).
- Entire M-02877 managed tree (diff -r on home-files): the ONLY differences are
  the 7 .md files gaining thinking: high on oracle/reviewer and the field
  reordering -- i.e. the store converging on what was already on disk. No other
  managed file changed.
- worldofgeese: identical managed file set; the only activation change is the
  removal of syncPiUserAgentModelOverrides.
- just check: exit 0. just fmt / check-fmt clean.

## Scope decisions

**The agent-shell elisp was folded in** (owner's call; this bead's criteria did
not mention it). Justified by evidence rather than assumption: Caveman Code's
~/.cave/agent/models.json on mahakala reaches http://127.0.0.1:8787 -- the exact
base URL modules/doom-emacs.nix already substitutes into the elisp -- using
eu.anthropic.claude-{opus-5,sonnet-5,haiku-4-5-...}. So the elisp's
anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 was stale for an endpoint known to serve the newer
ids. config.el now carries @GATEWAY_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL@ placeholders
substituted with --replace-fail. This DOES change runtime behaviour on mahakala
and is the one part of this change not covered by a byte-identical proof; it
needs verification there.

**fallbackModels is optional in the shared interface** (nullOr, default null), so
the personal profile's tier-defs.json keeps its two-key shape. Note that nothing
reads fallbackModels out of tier-defs.json -- the deleted script only ever read
model and thinking -- so it is inert data on the work profile, preserved only
because the byte-identical criterion required it.

**Not swept in**, as this bead instructed: the mkForce on beads-rust/governance
extensions and mcp.json (extension concerns, not tiers), the pi-rtk-optimizer
prohibition comment (left intact), models.json's seeded-once treatment.

## Filed rather than folded in

- home-manager-l23 (P1) -- ~/.cave/agent on mahakala is unmanaged and its
  models.json embeds a literal vk_ virtual key. Same credential class as 0pr.1.
  **The key was exposed in a session transcript; treat as compromised and
  rotate.**
- home-manager-8vh (P2) -- catalogue metadata disagrees between
  modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix (opus 1000000/128000) and
  ~/.cave/agent/models.json (opus 200000/32000). Only one can be mirroring the
  gateway's published catalogue. Needs the gateway's real catalogue as evidence,
  which no byte-identical criterion can supply.

## Deliberate omission in the patcher

The Node script also filtered *body* lines that exactly equalled a value it was
about to insert. The body begins after the only --- pair in these files, so no
such line has ever existed and the filter was unreachable. Not reproduced;
documented in modules/pi-tiers.nix so it does not look like an oversight.

## Shape delivered

modules/pi-tiers.nix (240 lines) owns the transform and the catalogue. Interface:
the pi.tiers.tiers option (a Home Manager option, deliberately not a den aspect
attribute -- den treats unrecognised aspect keys as child aspects) plus the
piTiers module argument carrying .slots and .models. No default on the tier
table: a machine opting into den.aspects.pi without one fails at eval.

Net: 6 files, +328/-238. modules/pi.nix 216 -> 97 lines; the ~50 lines of
embedded JavaScript and all 7 lib.mkForce on agent .md files are gone. Each
profile's table now sits with its profile (modules/worldofgeese.nix,
modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix).
close_reason: All five acceptance criteria met and verified from darwin: one module resolves tier->model with each profile contributing only its table, the Node activation patcher is deleted, zero mkForce remains on agent .md files, tier-defs.json and all 7 agent .md are byte-identical on both profiles against a reference oracle built from the deleted script, and just check exits 0. Deployment and the elisp's changed model ids are home-manager-dc7.

title: Give the model gateway one owner
description:
## Problem

Four modules each hold the complete set of facts about how an agent reaches a
model, and they have already drifted. There is no module that owns "the gateway".

| site | what it decides |
|---|---|
| `modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:71-173` | headroom `18787:8787`, `HEADROOM_MODE=cache`, `ANTHROPIC_TARGET_API_URL=…/claude`, local-model-proxy `18788:8788`, phoenix `16006:6006`, `MPS_BASE_URL`, `GATEWAY_IP` discovery, `/livez` gating |
| `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:88-99` | pi goes *direct* to `https://api.genai.thelegogroup.com/anthropic`, key via `!secretspec get …` |
| `guix/home-configuration.scm:208-244` | headroom `127.0.0.1:8787:8787`, `ANTHROPIC_TARGET_API_URL=…/claude`, **no `HEADROOM_MODE`**, different CLI flags |
| `modules/doom.d/modules/tools/agent-shell/config.el:44-45` | `http://127.0.0.1:8787` + a literal token |

Observed drift, all real today:

- `HEADROOM_MODE=cache` is set on macOS with a five-line rationale at
  `modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:71-75`. It is absent from
  `guix/home-configuration.scm:227-233`, so Linux silently runs headroom's
  built-in default mode. No error, just a different cost/cache-hit tradeoff.
- `8787` means "container-internal only" on macOS and "host and container" on
  Linux. A reader must already know which host they are on to interpret it.
- `docs/solutions/proxy-chain-and-harness-auth.md` documents a decommissioned
  backend (`models.assistant.legogroup.io`, "LEGO Model Proxy Service") and a
  `pi-extensions/anthropic-proxy` extension that was deleted in `6270a6c`. The
  provider name `anthropic-proxy` survives in `models.json` only as a string.
- `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`'s secretspec→`gh auth token` fallback is written
  twice, in two dialects: `modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:263-268` (sh, activation)
  and `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:546-556` (zsh, interactive init).

Churn evidence: 7 of the last 25 commits touch this addressing — `43fffae`,
`c8dcad6`, `6270a6c`, `6fe214d`, `121e567`, `3b0a8b5`, `14be3f0`, `50a3e40`.

## Why depth helps here

Two genuine adapters already exist for the same interface — a launchd adapter on
darwin and a shepherd/OCI adapter under Guix Home — so the seam is real, not
hypothetical. What is missing is the interface they should both satisfy.

## Shape to aim for (not prescriptive — grill it first)

A `den.aspects.gateway` (name it in `CONTEXT.md` when chosen) whose interface is
small and declarative, e.g.:

```
gateway = {
  baseUrl        = "https://api.genai.thelegogroup.com";
  claudePath     = "/claude";      # headroom upstream
  anthropicPath  = "/anthropic";   # pi direct
  headroom = { hostPort = …; containerPort = 8787; mode = "cache"; image = …; };
  proxy    = { hostPort = …; containerPort = 8788; };
  phoenix  = { hostPort = …; containerPort = 6006; };
  keyRef   = "!secretspec get -f … LEGO_GATEWAY_API_KEY";
};
```

Consumers become adapters:

- **launchd adapter** — `modules/M-02877/darwin.nix` reads the attrset instead of
  spelling out ports and URLs in shell strings.
- **Guix Home adapter** — Scheme cannot import Nix. Cross the seam with generated
  data: have the gateway aspect emit a JSON/env file that
  `guix/home-configuration.scm` reads, *or* accept the duplication deliberately
  and add paired breadcrumb comments (the `kubernetes-helm`/`kind` pattern at
  `modules/workstation.nix:38-39` + `guix/home-configuration.scm:58-59`). Decide
  this explicitly and record it.
- **consumer adapter** — `models.json` (`modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:88-99`) and
  the agent-shell elisp both take `baseUrl` and `keyRef` from the aspect.

## Constraints and gotchas

- `models.json` is deliberately seeded once and never overwritten
  (`modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:88-93`) so `/model` can re-point it live. Do not
  turn it into a managed file without deciding that tradeoff on purpose.
- `ANTHROPIC_*` env vars are deliberately **not** set for Claude Code on darwin
  (`modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:194-196`): Claude Code's own `settings.json` `env`
  block overrides launchd. Preserve that decision.
- `GATEWAY_IP` is parsed at runtime from `container network inspect` output
  (`modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:129-135`) precisely because a container's own IP

title: Architecture deepening from 2026-08-01 review
description:
Deepening work surfaced by the architecture review of 2026-08-01, run with the
`improve-codebase-architecture` skill against `~/.config/home-manager` at den
rev `2040b613`.

## Shared vocabulary (use these words in every child issue)

From the `codebase-design` skill: **module** (anything with an interface and an
implementation), **interface** (everything a caller must know), **depth**
(behaviour per unit of interface), **seam** (where an interface lives),
**adapter** (a thing satisfying an interface at a seam), **leverage** (what
callers get from depth), **locality** (what maintainers get from depth).
The **deletion test**: if the module vanished, would complexity concentrate
(it was shallow) or spread (it earned its keep)?

Do not substitute "component", "service", "API", "layer", or "boundary".

## Repo-specific vocabulary

- **aspect** — `den.aspects.<name>` with `.nixos` / `.darwin` / `.homeManager` sub-attributes
- **host** — `den.hosts.<system>.<hostname>`; **home** — `den.homes.<system>.<user>` (standalone HM, no system management)
- **battery** — `den.batteries.*`, e.g. `define-user`, `primary-user`
- **substrate** — NixOS / nix-darwin / Guix System + Guix Home / nix-on-droid
- **tier** — a pi agent model class (`fast`, `balanced`, `deep`, …) defined in `modules/pi.nix`

## Fleet

| entity | substrate | wired via |
|---|---|---|
| mahakala (`worldofgeese`) | Guix System + Guix Home + standalone HM | `den.homes.x86_64-linux.worldofgeese` |
| M-02877 (`dktaohan`) | nix-darwin + HM | `den.hosts.aarch64-darwin.M-02877` |
| paphos (`kypris`) | NixOS | `den.hosts.x86_64-linux.paphos` |
| oracle | NixOS | raw `nixosSystem` in `modules/oracle/image.nix` — outside den |
| pixel-fold | nix-on-droid | raw `nixOnDroidConfiguration` in `modules/pixel-fold/system.nix` — outside den, and den has no nixOnDroid support yet (see child issue) |

## Ground rules for every child issue

- `just check` must pass before and after. It is the only automated gate (plus `.githooks/pre-commit`, which runs it).
- Formatting is alejandra: `just fmt`, verified by `just check-fmt`.
- Use the `Justfile` for updates/deploys, never raw nix/guix commands (see `AGENTS.md`).
- There is no `CONTEXT.md` and no `docs/adr/` yet. Create them lazily: a new
  domain term goes in `CONTEXT.md`; a load-bearing rejection goes in `docs/adr/`.
- Guix files are Scheme and cannot import Nix values. Any fact shared between
  substrates has to cross that seam as generated data (JSON/env file) or be
  duplicated deliberately with paired breadcrumb comments — the pattern already
  used for `kubernetes-helm`/`kind` (`modules/workstation.nix:38-39` +
  `guix/home-configuration.scm:58-59`).
- On a full `just deploy-mahakala`, Home Manager applies *after* Guix Home
  (`Justfile:11-17`), so HM silently wins any contested file. That rule is
  currently written nowhere.

## Child issues, in recommended order

1. Rotate + de-hardcode the agent-shell gateway credential (do first, security)
2. Give the model gateway one owner (top recommendation)
3. One tier-routing module instead of two
4. Derive `just check` from the entity registry
5. Rust/kernel pins as data, not regex-anchored text
6. Bring oracle into `den.hosts`
7. Decide pixel-fold's relationship to den (upstream gap)
8. Move include edges to the registry
9. Declare Guix/HM ownership per concern on mahakala
10. De-duplicate host and user literals

title: Explain 6 unlocked gen-prelude fetches per darwin eval
description: A nix eval of .#darwinConfigurations.M-02877 logged 'fetching github input github:sini/gen-prelude/<rev>' six times across two revs. gen-prelude appears nowhere in flake.lock (56 nodes, verified intact against HEAD: no removed, added, or dangling nodes) and nowhere in the repo's nix files or any tracked file. Unlocked fetches on the hot path cost network round-trips on every eval and cannot be cached. Two candidate explanations remain: nix resolves it outside the lock via some input (llm-agents from numtide is the prime suspect), or the log lines came from a concurrent nix process (two other agent sessions were running at the time). Resolve with nix flake metadata --json on a quiet machine.
acceptance_criteria: Source of the gen-prelude fetches identified; if genuinely on our eval path, it is locked or removed
notes:
SECOND CORRECTION 2026-09-19: the root-vs-user hypothesis is also disproven. gen-prelude is now fetched by scripts/check-drvpaths.sh running as dktaohan from the pre-commit hook, with no sudo involved. So it is neither concurrency (first theory) nor root eval (second theory). Remaining observation: 'darwin-rebuild build .#M-02877' fetched it 0 times, while 'darwin-rebuild switch .#M-02877' and check-drvpaths.sh (which evaluates all four host configurations) each fetch it 6 times across the same two revs. That points at which evaluation entry point / output attrset is forced, and at a non-M-02877 configuration owning the input. I have guessed wrong twice; the next person should run 'nix flake metadata --json' and bisect by configuration attribute rather than theorise.
--notes=ROOT-CAUSED 2026-09-19. Deterministic reproducer: nix eval --no-warn-dirty --option tarball-ttl 0 --raw '.#darwinConfigurations.M-02877.system.drvPath' -> 6 gen-prelude fetches, as dktaohan, no sudo, no concurrent nix client. All three earlier theories (concurrent sessions, root-vs-user eval, entry point) were artifacts of tarball-ttl (default 3600s) deciding whether a given eval re-resolves an unlocked input. MECHANISM: gen-prelude is an unlocked transitive input of den. Our flake.nix:10 declares a bare 'den.url = github:denful/den' with no input bindings, and den's node in flake.lock has keys ['locked','original'] with NO inputs key at all -- the only input in the lock in that state. den/nix/lib/schema.nix takes { inputs, ... } and documents that consumers must bind the gen-* family through THE HUB, not gen-schema directly, warning that pinning directly yields 'three revisions of gen-prelude and two of gen-schema in one lock'. Because we bind nothing, den resolves the family live on every eval past the TTL. FIX: declare the hub input on den in flake.nix so it lands in flake.lock, then verify with the reproducer above (expect 0 fetches) and a full darwin build. Not applied yet -- it changes flake inputs and needs a rebuild to verify.
--notes=CORRECTION to the ROOT-CAUSED note above: den is NOT the source, so that fix (bind den's hub input) is wrong. Evidence: 'nix flake show github:denful/den' fetches gen-prelude 0 times; den's entire flake.nix is 'outputs = _: import ./nix;' with NO inputs block (hence the empty inputs key in our lock -- that is correct, not a defect); and a gh code search across denful/den finds no getFlake and no fetchTree. The gen-prelude mentions in den are comments and a templates/ci/flake.lock, neither on our eval path. ELIMINATED SO FAR: concurrency; root-vs-user eval; tarball-ttl alone (fetches recur within the TTL window); den; ewm (normal git flake, properly locked with nixpkgs.follows); the flake registry (38 entries, no match); every flake.nix (264) and flake.lock (259) at store depth 2 -- none mention gen-prelude or rev da7056327e5f8312d73d51895039a1f319166cd4. STILL UNKNOWN: which input asks for it. The reproducer is reliable, so the next step is mechanical rather than theoretical: bisect by commenting out root inputs one at a time and re-running the reproducer, or run the eval under a trace to capture the call site. I have guessed wrong four times here; do not add another hypothesis without the bisect.
--notes=BISECT RESULTS 2026-09-19 (culprit still NOT identified; do not add hypotheses without a valid test).

RELIABLE REPRODUCER: nix eval --no-warn-dirty --option tarball-ttl 0 --raw '.#darwinConfigurations.M-02877.config.networking.hostName' -> 6 fetches, two revs (da705632 x2, 57881cb5 x4). A trivial scalar option is enough, so the fetch is in base flake/module composition, not in any heavy derivation.

NEWLY ELIMINATED:
- doom/emacs path: the scalar eval above fetches gen-prelude 6x with 0 doom package fetches.
- All 18 root inputs resolved individually with tarball-ttl 0: 0 fetches each. CAVEAT: nix flake metadata only resolves locks, it never evaluates outputs, so this method is structurally blind to eval-time fetches. Do not treat it as clearance for getFlake-style fetching.
- den + flake-parts + import-tree composed in a minimal throwaway flake with pinned revs (VALID test: LOCK_RC=0, 6 nodes, EVAL_RC=0, eval returned a value): 0 fetches. So merely composing den does not trigger it.
- Our own repo: 0 occurrences of sini, getFlake, fetchTree, gen-prelude in any tracked file.
- .decapod/workspaces nested flakes: no sini refs, and the path is gitignored so nix never copies it.
- den itself: no getFlake/fetchTree anywhere except templates/noflake/npins; templates are declared as plain templates.<name>.path and are never evaluated. den's flake is 'outputs = _: import ./nix' with no inputs block, so the empty inputs key in our lock is correct.
- decapod, ewm, the flake registry (38 entries), and all store flake.nix (264) / flake.lock (259) at depth 2.
- flake.lock is NOT mutated by the reproducer, so nix is not trying and failing to persist a node.

ORIGIN OF THE REVS: both are pinned across sini/* repos (sini/gen, sini/gen-scope, sini/gen-aspects, sini/nix-config). den's templates/ci/flake.nix declares gen.url = github:sini/gen, but that template is not on our eval path.

TWO INCONCLUSIVE ATTEMPTS, flagged so nobody trusts their zeros: (1) a first isolation test whose nix flake lock was interrupted before completing -- its '0 fetches' means nothing was evaluated; (2) an attempt to force den.aspects in the isolated flake that errored on invalid aspect syntax (RC=1) before exercising the machinery.

NEXT STEP, mechanical: the trigger is in our modules/ or in one of the other 14 inputs when composed. Bisect import-tree over subsets of modules/ (copy the repo to /tmp and halve the module set against the reproducer), or force den.aspects correctly in the isolated flake using a real aspect from modules/terminal.nix as the template.
--notes=NEW OBSERVATION 2026-09-19 from a pre-commit hook run: the 6 gen-prelude fetches land immediately after 'fetching path input path:/Users/dktaohan/.config/home-manager' and immediately BEFORE the ~130 doom emacs package git inputs -- i.e. during our own flake's input-resolution phase, not during any derivation. This recurs once per nix invocation (check-drvpaths.sh and check-doom-darwin each produced their own set of 6 in the same 'just check' run). Combined with the earlier finding that a scalar option eval also produces 6 with zero doom fetches, the fetch is part of resolving our flake's inputs. Since gen-prelude appears nowhere in our lock and the lock is never mutated by the eval, a plausible remaining mechanism is nix resolving an input that a transitive dependency declares before a follows override discards it -- known to happen in some nix/lix versions. Worth checking against Lix 2.95.2 (nix.package = pkgs.lixPackageSets.latest.lix) release notes and issue tracker before more local bisecting.
close_reason: NOT A DEFECT. The premise was wrong: these are local cache resolutions, not network fetches. Nix prints 'fetching github input' when it RESOLVES a flake input regardless of whether the network is touched. Proof: the eval completes successfully with --offline, which forbids network access, and still logs all 6 lines. Timings for the same valid eval (nix eval '.#darwinConfigurations' --apply 'x: builtins.attrNames x', rc=0): --offline 769ms / default tarball-ttl 489ms / --option tarball-ttl 0 491ms, all with 6 lines. Forcing revalidation costs nothing measurable, so nix is not revalidating over the network. No /nix/store/*gen-prelude* path exists because the resolution lives in the content-addressed fetcher cache rather than a named store path. CONCLUSION: log noise, not a performance problem. Nothing to fix; the original worry (uncacheable network round-trips on every eval) is disproven. Which input declares it remains unidentified and is now cosmetic. Method note for future work: SIX hypotheses died here (concurrency, root-vs-user eval, tarball-ttl expiry, den unbound, den-in-composition, the doom path) and two --override-input tests produced meaningless zeros because the eval errored before the fetch (rc=1, no value). Any bisect of eval-time behaviour MUST assert the eval succeeded and returned a value; a zero from a failed eval is not evidence. The earliest valid trigger is forcing attrNames of darwinConfigurations, i.e. output-attrset construction.

title: The pre-commit gate is not actually installed; core.hooksPath is unset
description:
## Problem

home-manager-0pr's ground rules and several bead notes assert that
`.githooks/pre-commit` runs `just check` on every commit, and treat that as the
automated gate backing every change in the epic.

It does not run. `.githooks/pre-commit` exists and is executable, but
`core.hooksPath` is empty and `.git/hooks/pre-commit` does not exist, so git never
invokes it. Nothing has been gated by it in this clone.

Discovered while committing home-manager-0pr.3, whose `just check` runs were all
manual.

## Why it matters

The epic leans on this hook as the reason `just check` cannot be skipped. Every
bead that says 'just check must pass before and after (plus .githooks/pre-commit,
which runs it)' is describing a gate that is opt-in per clone and currently off.
It compounds home-manager-0pr.4, which is about that gate's *coverage*: coverage
gaps matter less than a gate that never fires.

## Shape to aim for

`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is the one-line fix, but it is per-clone
and therefore exactly the kind of fact that goes stale. Prefer something a fresh
clone gets for free -- the repo already builds developer environments, so wiring
it where those are defined is likely better than documenting a command someone
must remember to run on each machine.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh clone has the hook active without a manual step, or the manual step is
  documented somewhere a fresh clone will actually read.
- Verified by attempting a commit that fails `just check` and watching it be
  rejected.
- The claims in home-manager-0pr and its children are corrected if the mechanism
  ends up different from what they describe.

## Notes

Check the other four machines too: the hook's absence here says nothing about
whether it is wired on mahakala, paphos, oracle, or pixel-fold.
notes:
## Correction to this bead's suggested shape

The 'Shape to aim for' above is wrong: it proposes wiring core.hooksPath into the
developer environment as if no mechanism existed. One already does.

`just install-hooks` (Justfile) does exactly the job:

    cp .githooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit
    chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

So this is not missing machinery, it is an uninvoked recipe. Nothing in AGENTS.md,
CONTEXT.md or the epic mentions running it, which is why it was never run in this
clone. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` would be a *second*, competing
mechanism -- do not add it without retiring install-hooks first.

Reframes the work as: make the existing recipe unmissable (document it as a
first-run step, or have something already run per clone invoke it), and check
whether it was ever run on the other four machines. Do not build a new hook
installer.
close_reason: Gate is now armed and self-installing via just check -> install-hooks (31e34b2); rejection and pass both verified through the hook. Remaining per-machine audit is not actionable from this workstation and is captured in the comment.

comments.author: Tao Hansen
comments.text: Armed in this clone and made mechanical: Justfile 'check' now depends on 'install-hooks' (31e34b2), so running the documented gate installs .git/hooks/pre-commit instead of relying on memory. No competing core.hooksPath mechanism added. Verified rejection: staged syntax error in modules/paphos/system.nix -> commit failed with "error: undefined variable 'this-is-not-nix'" and "recipe check failed on line 175". Verified pass: the Justfile commit itself ran full just check through the hook (all five host evals + check-fmt) before landing. title: Declare Guix Home vs Home Manager ownership per concern on mahakala
description:
## Problem

mahakala is managed by three things at once — Guix System (`guix/system.scm`),
Guix Home (`guix/home-configuration.scm`), and a standalone Nix Home Manager
profile (`den.homes.x86_64-linux.worldofgeese`). Some of the split is forced.
Some of it is accidental, and resolved only by `$PATH` order.

**Forced by the substrate split — leave alone:**

- shepherd services: Guix has an init system, HM here does not
  (`guix/home-configuration.scm:246-266` signet-daemon, `:208-244` headroom)
- `~/.bashrc` ownership: Guix owns it (`guix/home-configuration.scm:121-125`,
  `guix/bashrc:21-25`); HM deliberately writes a *sourceable fragment* instead
  (`modules/shared-devtools.nix:56-59`). This is a well-designed seam — do not
  disturb it.
- `gpg-agent` (`guix/home-configuration.scm:170-178`) — HM has no equivalent here
- user `nix.conf` `experimental-features` vs system substituters
  (`guix/home-configuration.scm:285-296`, `guix/system.scm:31-59`) — self-documented

**Accidental — two providers, `$PATH` decides silently:**

| binary | Guix | Nix |
|---|---|---|
| `git` | `guix/home-configuration.scm:30` | `modules/git-common.nix:5-6` (configures it too) |
| `fd` | `:31` | `modules/doom-emacs.nix:22` |
| `openssh` | `:32` | `modules/ssh.nix:7` |
| `tmux` | `:34` | `modules/terminal.nix:61-88` (configures it too) |
| `ripgrep` | `:44` | `modules/doom-emacs.nix:21` |
| `pinentry-gnome3` / `gnupg` | `:60` | `modules/doom-emacs.nix:23-24` |
| `emacs` / `emacsclient` | `guix/system.scm:158` (`emacs-pgtk`, the EWM session Emacs, hardcoded at `guix/system.scm:117-118`) | `modules/doom-emacs.nix:15-26,118-127` (the daily driver) |

`EDITOR`/`VISUAL` are the bare string `"emacsclient"`
(`guix/home-configuration.scm:470,475`), so which Emacs answers depends entirely on
`$PATH` order, which is set by the same Guix service at
`guix/home-configuration.scm:465` (HM's profile prepended).

**Two fontconfig stacks that include each other rather than one winning:**
`guix/home-configuration.scm:352-461` hard-assigns `monospace → JetBrains Mono`
(`:400-414`); `modules/worldofgeese.nix:35-46` exposes Guix's font dirs back into
Nix's fontconfig; `modules/doom-emacs.nix:104-127` builds a third, private one for
its own binaries. Meanwhile `modules/terminal.nix:96-98` hardcodes
`FiraCode Nerd Font` for WezTerm — a different answer to "default monospace".

**Precedence is emergent, not stated.** `Justfile:11-17` runs `guix home
reconfigure` (`:15`) then `home-manager switch` (`:16`), so HM wins any contested
file on a full deploy. That rule appears in no document.

## The pattern already proven in this repo

`kubernetes-helm`, `kind` and `yt-dlp` were already de-duplicated using paired
breadcrumb comments naming the winner on both sides:
`modules/workstation.nix:38-39` + `guix/home-configuration.scm:58-59`
("consolidated to Nix HM workstation aspect"), and `modules/workstation.nix:42` +
`guix/home-configuration.scm:112` (yt-dlp stays in Guix). Reuse it verbatim.

## Work

1. For each accidental duplicate above, pick the owner and delete the other copy,
   leaving paired comments. Suggested default: the substrate that also *configures*
   the tool owns it (so `git`, `tmux` → Nix).
2. The `emacs` collision is the sharpest one: the EWM session needs Guix's
   `emacs-pgtk` at an absolute path (`guix/system.scm:117-118`), while the user
   wants Doom for editing. Decide explicitly whether `emacsclient` on `$PATH`
   should be Doom's, and write it down.
3. Pick one default monospace face and make WezTerm and fontconfig agree, or state
   why they differ.
4. Write the ownership rule and the HM-applies-last rule into `README.md` beside
   the existing prose at `README.md:295-299` and `:344-346`.

## Constraints and gotchas

- `~/.ssh` is a *real* historical conflict with compensating code on both sides:
  `guix/home-configuration.scm:126-145` chmods and skips symlinks;
  `modules/ssh.nix:58-67` forces a real file via activation. Documented at
  `README.md:344-346`. Do not touch it in this bead.
- `FONTCONFIG_FILE` is deliberately coordinated: `modules/worldofgeese.nix:25-33`
  patches Helium's wrapper from `--set` to `--set-default` specifically so it does
  not clobber Guix's global value (`guix/home-configuration.scm:467`). Preserve
  that, and note the trap for any future Nix GUI app.
- `podman` runtime config is Guix-only (`guix/system.scm:261-270`); Nix modules are
  pure consumers (`modules/workstation.nix:136`, `modules/shared-devtools.nix:169,183,226,229`).
  Not a duplication.
- Guix has no automated check (see the check-coverage bead), so changes here are
  verified by deploying. Deploy Guix Home and HM separately
  (`just deploy-mahakala-guix`, `just deploy-mahakala-hm`) so a failure is attributable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every binary in the accidental table has one provider, or a paired comment on
  both sides saying why it has two.
- `which -a emacs emacsclient git tmux fd rg` on mahakala returns one path each
  (or a documented, intended two).
- Default monospace is one decision.
- `README.md` states the ownership rule and that HM applies last.
- `just check` passes; `just deploy-mahakala-guix` then `just deploy-mahakala-hm`
  both succeed on mahakala.

title: Move include edges to the registry; retire single-consumer aspects
description:
## Problem

Include edges are scattered across the files they affect least, so no single file
answers "what does this machine get?".

**The bounce path for one question — "does `dktaohan` get `kubectl`?"**

1. `modules/hosts.nix:3` — `den.hosts.aarch64-darwin.M-02877.users.dktaohan = {}`
2. `modules/M-02877/dktaohan.nix:3-9` — `includes = [ … den.aspects.pi … ]`; no
   mention of `sharedDevtools` or `workstation`
3. `modules/pi.nix:6` — `includes = [den.aspects.sharedDevtools]` ← dev tooling
   arrives as a side effect of an **agent-harness** aspect
4. `modules/shared-devtools.nix:5-6` — `includes = [den.aspects.devtools]`
5. `modules/overlays.nix:6` — `den.aspects.devtools.homeManager`

And the comment at `modules/shared-devtools.nix:4` actively misleads: it says
"Host-specific additions go in workstation.nix or dktaohan.nix", while
`dktaohan.nix` never names `sharedDevtools` at all.

**Other misplaced edges**

- `den.aspects.server` (`modules/server.nix`) has exactly one consumer, and that
  consumer's include lives in a third file: `modules/defaults.nix:10-12`
  (`den.aspects.paphos.includes = [den.aspects.server]`). Deletion test:
  **concentrates** — inline it and nothing is lost.
- `den.aspects.worldofgeese` (`modules/worldofgeese.nix`) declares only git +
  home basics; its real content — `workstation` and `ssh` — is included from
  `modules/mahakala.nix:1-6`, a *host*-named file. The mirror image of the
  M-02877 layout, where `dktaohan.nix` is self-contained. Two conventions, one repo.
- `den.aspects.kypris` is a stowaway at the bottom of
  `modules/paphos/system.nix:49-56`, after ~48 lines of unrelated boot/sudo config
   — while `dktaohan` gets a whole file of its own.
- `den.aspects.paphos` is assembled across six files: `modules/defaults.nix:10-12`,
  `modules/paphos/{hardware,networking,forgejo,ops,system}.nix`. Splitting by
  concern is fine; the seventh touchpoint in `defaults.nix` for a single
  `includes` line is not.

## Shape to aim for

`modules/hosts.nix` becomes the registry that answers membership: every host,
every home, and its includes. Aspects hold **content only** and never include a
sibling aspect to obtain packages. Reading one file tells you what a machine gets;
reading one aspect tells you what that aspect contributes.

Two shallow aspects likely dissolve in the process (`server`, and possibly
`mahakala` as a separate file). Apply the deletion test to each before removing it:
does complexity concentrate, or spread?

## Constraints and gotchas

- `modules/defaults.nix` legitimately owns `den.default.*` and `den.schema.*`
  (`:6-8`) — the `define-user` battery, the `homeManager` user class, the default
  `stateVersion`. Leave those; only the `paphos.includes` edge is misplaced.
- den's aspect resolution is order-sensitive in places (route/forward ordering
  fixes landed in den PRs #574, #584, #603, #643). Move edges, do not reorder
  content inside an aspect.
- `import-tree ./modules` auto-discovers every file (`flake.nix`), so file renames
  are free but a file must not stop declaring what other files reference.
- The transitive `pi → sharedDevtools` edge is the one substantive behaviour change
  in this bead: removing it may change what `dktaohan` receives. Diff the package
  lists on both profiles and treat any difference as a decision, not a side effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Membership for every entity is readable from `modules/hosts.nix` alone.
- No aspect includes another aspect merely to obtain packages.
- The misleading comment at `modules/shared-devtools.nix:4` is true or gone.
- `den.aspects.kypris` lives in its own file.
- Package lists for `worldofgeese`, `dktaohan` and `kypris` are unchanged, or each
  difference is explained in the commit message.
- `just check` passes.

## Verification

```
for h in worldofgeese; do
  nix eval --no-warn-dirty --json ".#homeConfigurations.$h.config.home.packages" \
    --apply 'ps: builtins.sort (a: b: a < b) (map (p: p.name) ps)' > /tmp/$h.before
done
nix eval --no-warn-dirty .#darwinConfigurations.M-02877.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath > /tmp/darwin.before
# … make the change, re-run, diff …
just check
```

title: Decide pixel-fold's relationship to den (no nixOnDroid support upstream)
description:
## Problem, and the upstream constraint

`pixel-fold` (nix-on-droid) is built by a raw
`inputs.nix-on-droid.lib.nixOnDroidConfiguration` call in
`modules/pixel-fold/system.nix:1-43`, outside den, pointed at `./_home.nix`
(`:36`). Because it cannot include `den.aspects.*`, shared facts are re-typed:

| concern | pixel-fold | the aspect it duplicates |
|---|---|---|
| git identity | `modules/pixel-fold/_home.nix:39-44` | `modules/worldofgeese.nix:52-62` + `modules/git-common.nix:5-17` |
| ssh hosts `loving-kypris`, `paphos` | `:80-87` (lowercase `hostname` option style) | `modules/ssh.nix:17-24` (capitalised `HostName` style) |
| tmux | `:25-37` (own colour scheme, different plugins) | `modules/terminal.nix:61-88` |
| starship | `:8-23` | `modules/worldofgeese.nix:64-70` |

**Upstream status — den does not support nix-on-droid yet.**
https://github.com/denful/den/discussions/517 (opened 2026-05-12) asks for it.
Maintainer `sini` replied 2026-05-12: it "would 100% be feasible to implement with
the current mechanisms", a template demonstrating it "would be a fantastic
addition", and they would review and merge a PR. Suggested prior art: the
`fleet-demo` (changing host resolution paths / alternative targets), the `microvm`
templates (forwarding a host configuration into a subkey), and `terranix-demo`
(using host info to build a non-NixOS configuration). They offered real-time help
on Matrix and said they would otherwise pick it up "in a few weeks". As of den
`2040b613` (2026-07-31) there is still no nixOnDroid class, battery, or template.

There is a second, independent constraint: pixel-fold pins its own nixpkgs and
home-manager (`nixpkgs-nod`, `home-manager-nod` in `flake.nix`) because
nix-on-droid needs tested versions — see `README.md:301-305` and
https://github.com/nix-community/nix-on-droid/issues/495. Even with a den
nixOnDroid class, aspects that assume the root `nixpkgs` would not transfer
unchanged.

## This bead is a decision, then a small piece of work

Pick one, record it, then do it:

**A. Write the den `nixOnDroid` class ourselves and upstream it.**
Highest leverage, real cost. `den.schema` supports user-defined classes; the
`fleet-demo`/`microvm`/`terranix-demo` templates are the models. Would make
pixel-fold a first-class `den.hosts` entry and is a welcome upstream contribution.
Risk: the input-pinning problem remains — the class must let the entity carry its
own nixpkgs/home-manager.

**B. Keep pixel-fold outside den, but stop re-typing facts.**
Extract the shared data (git identity, the two tailnet SSH hosts) into a plain
Nix data module both graphs import — no den machinery involved. Cheap, removes the
drift, keeps two option dialects. Then record an ADR: *"pixel-fold stays outside
the den aspect graph because den has no nixOnDroid class (discussion #517) and
nix-on-droid requires pinned nixpkgs/home-manager (issue #495)"* — precisely so a
future architecture review does not re-suggest it.

**C. Wait for upstream.** Only defensible if paired with B's data extraction;
otherwise the drift keeps growing.

Recommendation: **B now, A as a separate opt-in bead.** B is small, removes the
actual pain (one place to rotate a key or rename a host), and the ADR stops the
suggestion recurring. A is a genuine upstream contribution and should be scoped on
its own merits, not smuggled into a de-duplication task.

## Acceptance criteria (for B)

- Git identity and the tailnet SSH host facts live in one data module, imported by
  both `modules/ssh.nix` / `modules/worldofgeese.nix` and
  `modules/pixel-fold/_home.nix`.
- `docs/adr/` exists with an ADR recording the decision, citing den discussion
  #517 and nix-on-droid issue #495.
- `CONTEXT.md` gains the term for whatever the data module is called.
- `nixOnDroidConfigurations.pixel-fold` still evaluates; `just check` passes.

## Verification

```
nix eval --no-warn-dirty --json .#nixOnDroidConfigurations.pixel-fold.config.system.stateVersion
just check
```

Note `just check` only forces `stateVersion` for pixel-fold (`Justfile:70`), so it
will not catch a package-list break here. See the check-coverage bead.

title: Bring oracle into den.hosts
description:
## Problem

`oracle` is a NixOS host built by a raw `inputs.nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem` call in
`modules/oracle/image.nix:1-14`, entirely outside den. It is therefore invisible
from the registry (`modules/hosts.nix` lists only `worldofgeese`, `M-02877`,
`paphos`) and cannot include any `den.aspects.*`. Everything a shared aspect
exists to centralise has been hand-copied instead, and has already diverged:

- **SSH hardening**: `modules/paphos/networking.nix:3` includes
  `den.aspects.ssh-server`, whose body (`modules/ssh.nix:70-78`) sets
  `PasswordAuthentication = false; PermitRootLogin = "no";` plus
  `services.tailscale.enable = true`. `oracle` re-states the same two settings at
  `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix:89-94` with **`PermitRootLogin = "prohibit-password"`**
  — a different answer to the same question, and nothing flags it.
- **Tailscale**: `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix:46-52` has its own block with
  peer-relay flags the shared aspect does not know about, including a hardcoded
  `--relay-server-static-endpoints=158.180.52.169:40000` (`:52`).
- **GitHub SSH keys**: `import ../_github-ssh-keys.nix pkgs` copy-pasted at
  `modules/paphos/system.nix:3` and `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix:7`.
- **`stateVersion`**: `"25.11"` typed independently at
  `modules/paphos/system.nix:5` and `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix:9`.
- **`den.aspects.server`** (`modules/server.nix`) — nix settings, GC policy,
  `gitMinimal`/`vim`, `services.openssh.enable` — is exactly what oracle wants and
  cannot have. It currently has a single consumer, wired from a third file
  (`modules/defaults.nix:10-12`).

Also, because `just check` only forces `stateVersion` for oracle
(`Justfile:60`), a package-list regression there is invisible.

## Work

1. Declare `den.hosts.aarch64-linux.oracle` (confirm the system — the image is
   built for `aarch64-linux`, see `Justfile:133`) in `modules/hosts.nix`.
2. Move `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix` content into
   `den.aspects.oracle.nixos`, and include `den.aspects.server` and
   `den.aspects.ssh-server`.
3. Reconcile the two divergent answers deliberately: either oracle keeps
   `prohibit-password` with a stated reason, or it adopts `"no"`. Decide, do not
   let the aspect silently overwrite it.
4. Keep the `nixosConfigurations.oracle` output name stable — `Justfile:40`
   (`deploy-oracle`) and `Justfile:60` (`check`) both reference it, and it is the
   name used for remote deploys.
5. Keep the image package working: `modules/oracle/image.nix` also produces
   `packages.aarch64-linux.oracle-image`, checked by `Justfile:133-134` and
   consumed by terraform (`terraform/oracle/variables.tf:41-44`).

## Constraints and gotchas

- den bumped to `2040b613` on 2026-08-01, which includes PR #643's fix for
  `{ user, … }` being silently dropped on standalone homes. Not directly relevant
  to a host, but relevant if you add a user aspect.
- Oracle is a remote aarch64 machine; `deploy-oracle` (`Justfile:40-41`) does
  **not** run `just update` first and has no comment explaining why. `deploy-darwin`
  documents the same choice at `:43-47` (do not couple a deploy to a 15-input
  flake update). Add the missing comment while you are here.
- oracle's public IP `158.180.52.169` appears in four places — see the
  host-literals bead. Do not fix that here; just do not add a fifth.

## Acceptance criteria

- `modules/hosts.nix` lists oracle; `rg 'nixosSystem' modules/` shows no raw
  system builder for it.
- `nixosConfigurations.oracle` still evaluates and the closure is equivalent
  (compare `system.build.toplevel.drvPath` before/after; any difference must be
  explained line by line).
- `PermitRootLogin` divergence is either removed or commented with its reason.
- `packages.aarch64-linux.oracle-image` still evaluates (`just check-oracle-image`).
- `just check` passes.

## Verification

```
nix eval --no-warn-dirty .#nixosConfigurations.oracle.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath   # capture before AND after
just check-oracle-image
just check
```
close_reason: Landed 12b22c6: oracle is in den.hosts with server + ssh-server, no raw nixosSystem builder remains, the image output is unchanged, and the only closure delta is git-minimal + vim from the server aspect. PermitRootLogin divergence is now explicit with a written reason.

comments.text:

Acceptance criteria:

- Closure delta explained line by line: toplevel drvPath nh98adpq… -> ply28070…. Comparing the two derivations, only three inputDrvs differ by hash (system-path, etc, activate) and no inputs were added or removed at the top level. system-path gains exactly git-minimal-2.55.0 and vim-9.2.0782, from den.aspects.server's environment.systemPackages. etc and activate have byte-identical input sets to before; they differ only because each references the new system-path. title: Set HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN: /v1/* is unauthenticated on non-loopback bind
description: Headroom container logs warn: 'non-loopback bind with NO token — /v1/* is UNAUTHENTICATED (set HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN)'. HEADROOM_HOST=0.0.0.0 is required so local-model-proxy can reach it across the proxy-chain network, but port 18787 is also published to the host, so any local process can drive the proxy. Fix: set HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN in modules/M-02877/darwin.nix and pass the matching credential from local-model-proxy, or stop publishing 18787 to the host if the gateway-IP path makes it unnecessary.
close_reason: Not needed: measured exposure is LAN-readable usage/cost telemetry plus DoS, not credential disclosure. The token option would 401 the live omp -> local-model-proxy -> headroom chain and cannot be satisfied by MPS; the loopback-publish option forces MPS onto churning container IPs. Evidence and the exact revisit recipe are in the comment.

comments.author: Tao Hansen
comments.text:
Investigated 2026-08-27 from M-02877 (LAN 192.168.99.156), probed off-host from LovingKypris 192.168.99.134. Not implemented — user judged the residual risk acceptable. Evidence below so this does not need re-deriving.

Actual exposure (headroom published 0.0.0.0:18787, confirmed '*.18787 LISTEN'):
- reachable off-host: /livez 200, /readyz 200, /docs 200, /openapi.json 200, /metrics 200, /stats 200, /quota 200, /dashboard 200
- /stats leaks usage and cost telemetry: request counts, primary model id, tokens before/after, cost with/without headroom in USD, per-agent labels
- /v1/messages without a credential returns 401, and /v1/models 401: headroom holds no gateway key (its env has ANTHROPIC_TARGET_API_URL only), so the caller must supply their own. No key theft path.
- /admin/runtime-env 503, /admin/upstream 404, /cache/clear 404, /settings 404, /settings/schema 404: no admin or destructive surface answered.
- phoenix is also published on all interfaces (*.16006 LISTEN) and has no auth, so OTel traces are LAN-readable too.
Net risk: LAN-readable cost/usage telemetry, plus DoS of a load-bearing local proxy. Not credential disclosure.

Why the bead's first option (set HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN) is infeasible as written, from headroom source (headroomlabs-ai/headroom 0.36.5):
- the gate exempts loopback callers entirely (proxy/server.py:3588), so agent-shell and host harnesses on 127.0.0.1 would be unaffected either way
- the only non-loopback caller is local-model-proxy, which reaches headroom at the container-network gateway 192.168.64.1:18787 (verified ESTABLISHED 192.168.64.3 -> 192.168.64.1.18787)
- the token is read from 'Authorization: Bearer' first, else 'X-Headroom-Proxy-Token' (server.py:2608-2620). Authorization is dual-purpose: consumed by the gate AND forwarded upstream, since only x-headroom-* is stripped (helpers.py:1635). local-model-proxy forwards its client's Authorization, which is the gateway key, so headroom would 401 every request unless the two secrets were byte-identical. MPS exposes no header-injection env (inspected: PROXY_HOST/PORT, MPS_BASE_URL, LOG_LEVEL, PRICING_PLAN, OTEL_*).
- this matters because omp is actively using that chain right now: lsof shows omp pid 46581 -> 127.0.0.1:18788 -> local-model-proxy -> headroom. Setting the token would have 401'd live traffic.

Why the bead's second option (stop publishing to the host) is available but was not taken:
- 'container run -p' accepts [host-ip:]host-port:container-port, and a loopback-only publish does close the LAN: a scratch container published on 127.0.0.1:19999 answered 200 on loopback and 000 from 192.168.99.156.
- but two host IPs cannot share one host port: 'Error: host ports for different publish port specs may not overlap', so loopback and 192.168.64.1 cannot both be published.
- Apple container 1.3.0 provides no inter-container DNS on this network ('headroom' and 'headroom.proxy-chain' both fail to resolve), while container-to-container by IP works (192.168.64.2:8787 -> 200). So a loopback-only publish forces MPS onto headroom's container IP, which is reassigned on restart — exactly the stale MPS_BASE_URL failure already documented in modules/M-02877/darwin.nix, and it would need a restart-coupling mechanism to stay correct.

If revisited: the change is host: "" -> "127.0.0.1" for headroom (and phoenix) under published.M-02877 in gateway.json, plus rewiring MPS_BASE_URL and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to container IPs resolved at MPS startup, plus something that restarts MPS when headroom's IP changes.
