title: U3: Re-plumb host integrations against the containerised daemon
description:
Reinstall each harness connector against the selected daemon entry point, re-point the Signet MCP server entry, and resolve transcript-capture and GraphIQ path visibility. An index built on host paths is useless to a container that mounts them elsewhere: either the mount path matches the host path or the index is rebuilt.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-28-001-signet-container-migration-and-docs-accuracy-plan.md (U3)
acceptance_criteria: A Claude Code session-start hook exits 0; the MCP server completes a tools/list handshake; transcript capture reports healthy; signet sources list shows 4 repos; GraphIQ status reports an active project.
notes:
Partial: the host CLI entry point is built; harness/MCP re-pointing is deliberately NOT flipped yet because it would break the native baseline Main is still comparing against.

Done: /app/bin/signet exported through distrobox. Command used:
  ~/.local/bin/distrobox-enter --name signet -- distrobox-export --bin /app/bin/signet --export-path /Users/dktaohan/.local/share/signet-distrobox/bin
Generated launcher is a POSIX sh script (not Mach-O), 370 bytes, of the expected shape:
  exec "/Users/dktaohan/.local/bin/distrobox-enter" -n signet -- "/app/bin/signet" "$@"
with the in-container and cross-container branches distrobox always emits. Exported to a staging path rather than ~/.local/bin because the native Mach-O ~/.local/bin/signet must survive until Main verifies parity. Cutover is a copy of that file to ~/.local/bin/signet, or a re-run of the same command with --export-path "$HOME/.local/bin". Note the launcher hardcodes the distrobox-enter it was generated with -- ~/.local/bin/distrobox-enter, which the launchd agent keeps refreshed -- so it does not depend on /opt/homebrew being visible.

Path visibility resolved without an index rebuild: distrobox already bind-mounts $HOME at the identical path (/Users/dktaohan:/Users/dktaohan), and this setup adds /var/folders at the identical path too. Host-indexed absolute paths therefore resolve unchanged inside the container, so GraphIQ project paths and source checkouts do not need re-indexing. Only the workspace itself is remapped (~/.agents -> /data/agents), which is a container-internal detail.

title: U2: Run the Signet daemon from a container on podman
description:
Start podman-machine-default and run ghcr.io/signet-ai/signet with ~/.agents bind-mounted at /data/agents, port published to host loopback only, and single-user auth pinned (the first-party entrypoint writes auth.mode: team on first run, which would break every local caller). Point the dreaming target endpoint at host.containers.internal:3851 for the gateway shim.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-28-001-signet-container-migration-and-docs-accuracy-plan.md (U2)
acceptance_criteria: curl -sf --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:3850/health/ready returns ready; agent.yaml auth mode is unchanged after first boot; container survives podman machine stop && start; 3850 is not reachable from a non-loopback interface.
notes:
Container built and proven on Podman (no Docker Desktop). NOT started/parity-tested here; left Exited so 127.0.0.1:3850 stays free for the controlled cutover.

Runtime: distrobox 1.8.2.5, container `signet` from pinned ghcr.io/signet-ai/signet:0.214.22 (linux/arm64, Debian trixie; works as a real distrobox box -- apt-get/useradd present, distrobox-init completed). Created with --unshare-netns --no-entry, --volume ~/.agents:/data/agents (the one existing workspace), --volume /var/folders:/var/folders, --additional-flags "--publish 127.0.0.1:3850:3850 --env SIGNET_DAEMON_ENTRYPOINT=0 --env SIGNET_PATH=/data/agents --env SIGNET_BIND=0.0.0.0 --env SIGNET_PORT=3850". podman inspect confirms PortBindings 127.0.0.1:3850 only. `signet --version` inside -> 0.214.22.

Four non-obvious things, all measured on this machine:

1. --unshare-netns is mandatory, not tuning. distrobox defaults to --network host; on macOS "host" is the podman VM, so --publish is silently inert and 3850 never appears on the mac.

2. Homebrew distrobox cannot be used directly. The podman VM shares only /Users, /private, /var/folders, /etc/containers -- /opt/homebrew is invisible. distrobox derives distrobox-init/-export/-host-exec from dirname($0) and bind-mounts them, so podman is asked to mount a path the VM cannot see. Fix: real copies (symlinks still resolve to /opt/homebrew) of /opt/homebrew/opt/distrobox/bin/distrobox* into ~/.local/bin, and invoke that copy.

3. distrobox-enter forwards the ENTIRE host environment, macOS TMPDIR=/var/folders/... included. Without --volume /var/folders:/var/folders every signet invocation dies in materializeEmbeddedAssetTree with EACCES mkdir "/var/folders". Mounting it at the identical path fixes it.

4. `distrobox assemble` is unusable on macOS: its ini parser runs sed "s/\s*$//g" and BSD sed reads \s as a literal s, so every value silently loses a trailing "s" (/data/agents arrived as /data/agent). The create call is driven directly from Nix instead.

Auth: agent.yaml is NOT clobbered. distrobox replaces the image entrypoint with distrobox-init, so /app/deploy/docker/entrypoint.sh (the auth.mode: team writer) never runs; and it only writes when agent.yaml is absent, which the bind mount prevents. Verified: still no auth block; diff against the U1 verified backup shows exactly one intended line changed (see below).

SIGNET_DAEMON_ENTRYPOINT: image sets it to 1 globally and signet routes ANY invocation to the daemon while it is 1, so the exported `signet status` would become a second daemon. Pinned to 0 in the container env; only the daemon exec line re-enables it (proven: env=1 turns `signet --version` into a daemon boot).

Dreaming reachability: agent.yaml inference.targets.lego.endpoint changed 127.0.0.1:3851 -> host.containers.internal:3851. Verified gvproxy proxies container->host loopback (a throwaway host listener on 127.0.0.1:3999 was reachable from the container as host.containers.internal:3999), so the gateway shim keeps its hardcoded 127.0.0.1 bind and its credential flow completely unchanged. Note the shim is currently DOWN independently of this work (launchctl shows com.dktaohan.signet-gateway-shim last exit 2, nothing listening on 3851) -- that predates the container and needs its own look.

Supervision declared in modules/M-02877/darwin.nix as launchd user agent com.dktaohan.signet-container: refreshes the $HOME distrobox copies, starts podman machine if down, creates the container if absent, then execs `distrobox-enter -- env SIGNET_DAEMON_ENTRYPOINT=1 /app/bin/signet`. RunAtLoad, KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false. It stands down (clean exit 0) while ai.signet.daemon.deede318fbb7 is still loaded, so two daemons can never share memories.db; deleting the native block in U5 hands ownership over with no further edit.

State for cutover: native ai.signet.daemon.deede318fbb7 is NOT loaded (launchctl print: no such service; startup.log empty). The native path actually in use is the npm install's mcp-stdio.js bun process. Also: `distrobox rm signet` deletes exported launchers -- do not export over ~/.local/bin/signet until ready.

Distrobox/podman container 'signet' runs ghcr.io/signet-ai/signet:0.214.27 with ~/.agents bind-mounted at /data/agents, --unshare-netns and --publish 127.0.0.1:3850:3850 (loopback only), SIGNET_DAEMON_ENTRYPOINT=0 so the first-party entrypoint never writes auth.mode: team, and ~/.agents/agent.yaml pointing dreaming at http://host.containers.internal:3851. Declarative unit: modules/M-02877/darwin.nix launchd agent com.dktaohan.signet-container. Verified: signet status --json -> version 0.214.27, probe healthy, /health/ready 200.

title: Declare pixel-fold in den.hosts with intoAttr = []
description:
## Why
pixel-fold is the last entity outside the registry: modules/pixel-fold/system.nix
calls inputs.nix-on-droid.lib.nixOnDroidConfiguration raw. Den has a supported way to
declare a host it does not build: intoAttr = [] (templates/microvm/modules/guests-example.nix:9,
contract at docs/reference/output.mdx:78, enforced in den's modules/policies/flake.nix:59-63,70-74).

Declaring den.hosts.aarch64-linux.pixel-fold = { intoAttr = []; } gives it a host
scope and makes it visible to anything iterating den.hosts, while system.nix keeps
emitting the real configuration.

## Do not attempt here
Having den actually build it. There is no nixOnDroid class anywhere in the pinned rev
(nix/lib/entities/host.nix:87-104,113-132 covers nixos/darwin/systemManager only), and
den unconditionally appends { nixpkgs.hostPlatform = lib.mkDefault spec.system; } to
the module list (nix/lib/aspects/fx/resolve.nix:292-293), which nix-on-droid's module
set does not declare. That is a separate project — see home-manager-0pr.7.

## Acceptance
- pixel-fold appears in den.hosts
- nixOnDroidConfigurations.pixel-fold still evaluates and its drvPath is unchanged
- just check passes

title: Publish the eval gate as flake.checks via den's checks class
description:
## Why
modules/checks.nix hand-rolls flake.evalChecks by mapping over four hardcoded
*Configurations attrsets. Den has a built-in checks class with a default-active route
to flake.checks.<system> (den's modules/policies/flake.nix:14-17,40-45,83,88-93;
documented docs/reference/policies.mdx:326 and docs/reference/output.mdx:104-140).
Present in the pinned rev. Publishing there makes plain 'nix flake check' cover the
gate instead of a bespoke nix eval invocation.

## Carry this forward verbatim or it becomes a downgrade
The reason checks.nix hashes package NAMES rather than forcing toplevel or
activationPackage: doom-emacs builds via IFD, so forcing the activation package for
the worldofgeese home makes eval *build* doom-intermediates, which needs a real
x86_64-linux builder that darwin does not have. The check must stay eval-forcing, not
a real build.

## Known limit
nixOnDroidConfigurations.pixel-fold is not a den entity, so it cannot emit a den
checks key until it is declared (see the intoAttr bead). Either sequence that first or
leave that one entity hand-rolled and say so.

## Acceptance
- nix flake check covers every entity the current evalChecks covers, or the gap is named
- the br-rename regression test still fails the gate (rename the br overlay attribute,
  expect failure, restore)
- just check still passes and its runtime does not regress materially
close_reason: Landed abf9af1: gate published as real flake.checks for all five entities, IFD-avoidance preserved, and a string-context defect fixed that would have made nix build of a check realise the whole system.

comments.author: Tao Hansen
comments.text:
Landed abf9af1. flake.evalChecks -> flake.checks.<system>.<entity>:
  aarch64-darwin: M-02877
  aarch64-linux:  oracle, pixel-fold
  x86_64-linux:   paphos, worldofgeese

Not implemented via den's checks aspect class (den.policies.checks-to-flake), and the bead's framing was wrong on that point. That class hands an aspect 'pkgs'; a whole-entity check needs the *instantiated* configuration, which is only reachable from the flake outputs. den's own templates/example/modules/tests.nix reads inputs.self.nixosConfigurations for exactly this reason. So the real win here was publishing to a standard output, not adopting the class.

IFD-avoidance carried over verbatim: still hashes package NAMES, never forces activationPackage. Comment retained and expanded in modules/checks.nix.

One defect found and fixed while doing it: embedding system.build.toplevel.drvPath in the report gave the check derivation string context on the whole system closure, so 'nix build .#checks.aarch64-darwin.M-02877' began realising all of M-02877 (observed: it started copying store paths from cache.nixos.org). builtins.unsafeDiscardStringContext fixes it — the check now has two inputDrvs (bash-5.3p15, stdenv-darwin-no-cc), builds instantly to a text file containing the drvPath and per-user digests, and eval still forces the drvPath. Without that, adopting flake.checks would have turned 'nix flake check' into a full system build.

just check now forces drvPaths across every system instead of running nix flake check, because four of five entities can only be evaluated here, not built. Noted in the recipe comment.

Acceptance: regression test re-run on the new output — renaming the br overlay attribute fails with 'while evaluating attribute x86_64-linux', exit 1. Coverage is the same five entities as before, pixel-fold included (it did not need to wait on anything, since the check reads the flake output rather than a den class). just check runtime unchanged in practice; the commit went through the pre-commit hook.

title: skills CLI records lowercase skills/ path for repos using Skills/, breaking update tracking
description: skills.sh CLI (v1.5.23) probes PRIORITY_PREFIXES with lowercase 'skills/'. On case-insensitive macOS FS the probe resolves against a repo whose real dir is 'Skills/' (e.g. sammcj/agentic-coding), so the lock records skillPath='skills/<n>/SKILL.md'. getSkillFolderHashFromTree() then does a case-SENSITIVE compare against the GitHub tree ('Skills/<n>') and returns null, leaving skillFolderHash empty. getSkipReason() reports the misleading 'Private or deleted repo' and topgrade's Skills step says the skills cannot be checked automatically. Worked around 2026-08-21 by rewriting ~/.local/state/skills/.skill-lock.json in place (48 entries case-corrected + tree SHAs stamped). Any future 'skills add' from such a repo will re-break.
notes: Upstream fix: make the tree lookup case-insensitive, or record the real path from the tree rather than the probe prefix. Report to skills.sh.

title: De-duplicate host and user literals (keys, oracle IP, openclaw host)
description:
## Problem

Facts that belong to one module are written down in several. None has bitten yet,
which is why this is the lowest-priority bead — but each one costs on the day it
changes.

**1. Five authorized keys, copy-pasted verbatim.**
`modules/paphos/hardware.nix:28-33` (initrd-stage SSH, port 2222) and
`modules/paphos/system.nix:27-32` (`users.users.kypris.openssh.authorizedKeys.keys`)
hold the identical 5-key block. Rotating or revoking a key needs both, and neither
file references the other. Note `system.nix:26` already demonstrates the better
pattern next door: `keyFiles = [worldogeeseGithubSshKeys]` via
`modules/_github-ssh-keys.nix`.
Deletion test: **concentrates** — one `let` binding or a shared
`modules/paphos/_keys.nix` removes it with no loss.

**2. One IP, four files, with the real source of truth elsewhere.**
`158.180.52.169` appears at `Justfile:40` (`deploy-oracle` host and build-host),
`modules/oracle/_configuration.nix:52` (`--relay-server-static-endpoints`, with a
hand-maintenance comment at `:49`), and `modules/ssh.nix:39` (`HostName`).
`terraform/oracle/outputs.tf:9-13` and `terraform/oracle/reserved_ip.tf:21-31` are
the actual source of truth once the reserved-IP resources are enabled, and
terraform never writes the value back.

**3. A host name inside a generically-named aspect.**
`modules/shared-devtools.nix:89-241` defines `openclaw-auth-loving-kypris()` with
`local host="loving-kypris"` hardcoded — a ~130-line shell function plus an
embedded Node SQLite script. It ships to every consumer of `sharedDevtools`, which
via `modules/pi.nix:6` means every consumer of `pi`, which means both mahakala and
M-02877, regardless of whether that machine ever SSHes into `loving-kypris`.
The file's own header (`:1-4`) frames itself as tooling shared across hosts.
Deletion test: **concentrates** — move it to the one host that needs it.

**4. A user name baked into a host aspect ~15 times.**
`den.aspects.M-02877` spells out `dktaohan` / `/Users/dktaohan` at
`modules/M-02877/darwin.nix:38` (`trusted-users`), `:41-42` (`users.users…home`,
`system.primaryUser`), across five launchd agent blocks at `:185-238`
(`GC_HOME`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `PATH`,
`WorkingDirectory`, `StandardOutPath`, `StandardErrorPath` for
`gascity-supervisor`, `nanoclaw-container-runtime`, `nanoclaw`), and `:247`
(sudoers). The same file already does the right thing for `config.homebrew.user`
in its `preActivation` block, so the pattern exists locally.

**5. Duplicated dependency list inside one derivation.**
`modules/overlays.nix:73-96` and `:113-136` — `mcp-agent-mail`'s ~25-package
`propagatedBuildInputs` re-typed verbatim inside the `postInstall`
`makePythonPath` call.

## Work

Each item is independent; do them as separate commits.

1. One key list, two consumers.
2. Decide the IP's owner. Cheapest honest fix: one Nix attribute both
   `modules/ssh.nix` and `modules/oracle/_configuration.nix` read, plus a comment
   pointing at the terraform output as upstream truth. Better: generate it from
   terraform output. Do not add a fifth copy.
3. Move the `openclaw-auth-*` function to the host aspect that needs it, and take
   the host name as an argument.
4. Derive user/home from `config.system.primaryUser` and
   `config.users.users.<u>.home` in the launchd blocks.
5. Bind the python dependency list once in a `let`.

## Constraints and gotchas

- The initrd SSH config (`modules/paphos/hardware.nix:26-33`) runs in a different
  stage than the login user's `authorizedKeys` and uses port 2222 — sharing the key
  *list* is safe; sharing anything else is not.
- Do not fold `_github-ssh-keys.nix` (a `keyFiles` fetch) into the literal key
  list; they are different mechanisms on purpose.
- Renaming the macOS primary user is not the goal — only removing the need to edit
  15 places if it ever happens. Keep the diff mechanical and verify the darwin
  closure is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each fact above is written once and read everywhere else.
- `nixosConfigurations.paphos` and `darwinConfigurations.M-02877` produce identical
  `system.build.toplevel.drvPath` before and after (this bead should be behaviour-
  preserving; any difference is a bug in the change).
- `just check` passes.

## Verification

```
nix eval --no-warn-dirty .#nixosConfigurations.paphos.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath   # before AND after, must match
nix eval --no-warn-dirty .#darwinConfigurations.M-02877.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath # before AND after, must match
rg -n '158\.180\.52\.169' . --glob '!.git'
just check
```
close_reason: Landed a08e3d4: paphos keys in _keys.nix, oracle's IP owned by oracle.json and read by both Nix and the Justfile, openclaw auth scoped to the workstation aspect. All three verified; docs updated.

comments.author: Tao Hansen
comments.text:
Landed a08e3d4. All three items done.

1. paphos authorized keys -> modules/paphos/_keys.nix, imported by both hardware.nix (initrd, port 2222) and system.nix (users.users.kypris). The two blocks were never identical and the asymmetry is deliberate, so the data file keeps them apart: 'remote' is the five keys both sites use, 'local' is kypris's own key on paphos, which is useless at initrd stage because you connect FROM another machine then. Verified: kypris still 6 keys, initrd still 5. Their order inside authorized_keys changes, which is semantically irrelevant there.

2. oracle's public IP -> oracle.json, read by modules/oracle/facts.nix (injected as the oracleHost module arg, same pattern as modules/gateway.nix) and by deploy-oracle, now a bash recipe computing its default from the same file. Verified identical: relay flags [--relay-server-port=40000, --relay-server-static-endpoints=158.180.52.169:40000], oracle-public HostName 158.180.52.169 user nixos, deploy default nixos@158.180.52.169. git grep finds no literal left outside oracle.json, terraform and one explanatory comment. docs/oracle/{how-to-deploy-and-peer-relay,reference-operations}.md now name oracle.json as the file to edit, and their stale modules/oracle/_configuration.nix references were fixed too (renamed in 12b22c6).

3. openclaw-auth-loving-kypris -> den.aspects.workstation as ~/.config/bash/extras.d/openclaw.bash; the shared integrations file sources that directory. Verified: worldofgeese has both files, dktaohan only the shared one. The bead's blast-radius note was stale in one detail: it said the function reached both machines via modules/pi.nix, which no longer exists; it reached them directly through sharedDevtools.

Process note, because it cost real time: a concurrent 'topgrade --yes' (pid 88116, running 1h36m) was mutating this repo. A stray 'git reset' from it landed between 'git add -A' and 'git commit', so the first attempt (3f17b0a) recorded an EMPTY commit while every change stayed in the working tree, and the following 'just check' then failed with "attribute 'oracleHost' missing" because modules/oracle/facts.nix was untracked and therefore invisible to the git+file flake. topgrade was also mid-regeneration of AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CODEX.md/GEMINI.md and .decapod state. Fixed by stopping topgrade, then amending. Those decapod-regenerated surfaces and an unrelated in-flight Signet LaunchAgent change in modules/M-02877/darwin.nix are deliberately NOT in this commit.
